requirements.statement: There is one set of k6 performance suites for INS. Which environment a run targets (local Docker stack, CDP dev, CDP test or CDP perf-test) is chosen by run configuration, never by a separate copy of a suite.
requirements.why: The ruling makes k6 the tool; the tests repo already names the CDP environments, so the suites reuse them rather than inventing new ones.
requirements.deltaNote: The tests repo already resolves base URLs per environment for Playwright (tests-005, tests-001-m1). k6 has nothing (tests-001).

requirements.statement: A tier-1 smoke run at smoke scale runs on every pull request and fails the pull request when a threshold fails.
requirements.why: Tier 1 answers whether a change made INS slower.

requirements.statement: The suites are organised by set, one Playwright project per journey set.
requirements.why: A k6 profile sits beside the existing projects rather than replacing them.
requirements.deltaNote: tests-002: the e2e, admin, ins and plants projects already exist.

requirements.statement: Tier 4 calls the real external systems directly at owner-agreed rates, never as a load test.
requirements.why: Only the conformance run touches real dependencies, and only at rates an owner agrees to.

requirements.statement: The DR records its status and the date it was agreed.
requirements.why: Document metadata, not behaviour the suites need.

requirements.statement: Inside the INS product boundary a run uses the real component; outside it, a stub configured from the agreed interface service level.
requirements.why: The boundary rule is what makes a result attributable to INS.
